lines.chapter: 1. Landing in Aruba: Queen Beatrix Airport
lines.text: Welcome to Aruba, and welcome to Queen Beatrix.
Queen Beatrix International Airport has frequent nonstop or one-stop flights from most major US cities, and daily flights from big hubs around the world.
Once you're off the plane, everyone clears immigration on arrival, and eligible travellers can use the e-gates to move a little faster.
Then customs: anything that may be prohibited, or subject to tax or duty, has to be declared.
From the air, you've already seen the colours, and the calm, turquoise west coast is where most visitors are heading.
Aruba sits in the southern Caribbean, just outside the hurricane belt, about fifteen to eighteen miles off the coast of Venezuela, and it's only six miles across.
The climate is tropical semi-arid: warm and sunny all year, with just the occasional brief shower.
Have you flown into Aruba before? Drop your best arrival tip in the comments; it genuinely helps the next traveller.
Now, the one bit of paperwork that matters before you even board.
Every traveller to Aruba, including infants and children, must complete the online ED-Card, the Embarkation and Disembarkation Card, and get it approved.
You can fill it in within seven days before your trip, and the airline will ask for proof of approval before you fly. Even passengers in transit need one.
Bring a valid passport. American, Canadian, Caribbean, European and most South American citizens don't need a visa, and British citizens can stay up to three months without one.
There's also a sustainability fee for visitors arriving by air, and the tourism authority keeps its traveller requirements page up to date, so check the current details there just before you go.
And sort out travel health insurance; the UK government notes that European and Global Health Insurance Cards aren't valid in Aruba.

lines.chapter: 3. Aruba Airport to Hotel: Transfer, Taxi or Rental
lines.text: Right, bags in hand. Where are you actually going?
Most hotels and resorts sit along the northwestern coast: the high-rises at Palm Beach, and the low-rise resorts near quieter Eagle Beach.

map.text: AUA → Oranjestad → Eagle Beach → Palm Beach

lines.text: Option one is the calmest: a pre-booked private transfer. You walk out of arrivals, your driver is waiting, and the first hour takes care of itself.

On aurum-transfers.com you can compare airport transfers from partner companies; the partner you choose runs the ride, so book once your flight times are fixed and keep the confirmation on your phone.
Option two, a taxi. The UK government's advice is simple: agree the fare with the driver, in local currency, before you set off.

lower.sub: Agree the fare before you set off

lines.text: Option three, a rental car, motorcycle or scooter, which you can pick up right at the airport.
Just check the small print first: rental companies often ask for two years of driving experience, a higher minimum age, or an international driving permit.

lines.chapter: 4. Aruba Beaches: Eagle Beach, Palm Beach and the Wild Coast
lines.text: Now the good part: the beaches.
The rule of thumb is simple. The west and south coasts are calm and protected, good for swimming and snorkelling.
The east and north coasts face the open sea, with stronger winds, crashing waves and big views.
Eagle Beach is the long stretch of soft white sand with the famous fofoti trees, and visitors are asked to treat them with respect.
Up the hotel strip, Palm Beach is where the high-rises meet the palapas. Want free shade under a public palapa? Arrive early.
Boca Catalina is a small bay with gentle waves and colourful reef fish just offshore.

lower.sub: Small, calm bay on the west coast

lines.text: Over on the east side, Boca Grandi suits windsurfing and kitesurfing, but its strong current makes it a poor place to swim.
Wherever you are, don't feed the wildlife, never stand on the reef, and leave shells and coral where you found them.
So, the short version. Get your ED-Card approved before you fly. Pick your ride before you land: transfer, taxi or rental. Swim on the calm west coast, and save the wild east for the views.
